summary: Managed Gmail read and inbox-v1 thread responses return links[]: inert {href,text} anchors extracted from text/html parts.

contract.read: GET /api/v1/eliza/google/gmail/read adds links: [{href,text}] (empty when there is no HTML part); older servers omit the field and clients treat it as []
contract.extraction: new pure module packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/utils/gmail-mime-text.ts: <a href> in text/html parts only, comments/script/style removed first, entities decoded, absolute http(s) without userinfo, href <= 2048, deduplicated by destination, at most 50, label reduced to plain text (<= 200 chars, hostname when empty)
contract.safety: nothing is fetched or rendered; plain-text URLs are left to the client (Alpha linkifies https URLs and reviews the origin before opening in its Browser)

dependencies: Tests ran with a scratch node_modules symlinked into the isolated worktree, containing only lockfile-pinned @electric-sql/pglite 0.4.6, drizzle-orm 0.45.3, hono 4.13.9, typescript 6.0.3, @types/bun 1.4.2 and @biomejs/biome 2.5.14; no full monorepo install. Files that import @elizaos/core, @elizaos/plugin-google-workspace or the database client (gmail.ts, shared.ts, inbox-managed.ts, google-mcp-shared.ts, the inbox-v1 and read routes) were checked with biome only; their full package typecheck and existing gmail.test.ts were not run because those packages are not installed in the scratch environment.
network: No Google network calls, accounts or credentials: a closed in-process fetch transport answers every provider request with synthetic data.
isolation: Authored as stacked commits on cd12fabd7bfada24f90f1d01e1a4dc8d1a4b095e in an isolated sparse worktree under the session scratchpad and re-applied in series to a second clean worktree; never applied to vendor/eliza.
upstreamPullRequest: Not opened; publishing to elizaOS needs the owner's explicit approval.
deployment: Not upstreamed and not deployed to Eliza Cloud. Clients detect the change only through the additive fields and capabilities above; until a reviewed merge and deploy, deployed servers omit them and Alpha keeps the older behavior.
